summary: Embedding prefetch worker starvation in rerank pipeline causing elevated P95 latency and partial result sets
description: Customer reports sudden increase in reranking tail latency (P95) and intermittent partial/empty candidate lists from the /v1/rerank endpoint. Issue began after a quiet client-side rollout of batch prefetching in the customer's SDK. Top-level symptom: rerank requests return 200 but with fewer than expected candidates or truncated lists; end-to-end P95 jumps from ~120ms to 750-1200ms for affected calls.
impact: Impacts subset of QleverSearch's production queries using Dedicated capacity in us-east-1. Customers report search relevance degradation when top-k results are missing. Estimated 18% of their rerank traffic is affected; revenue-affecting for search product. No token billing discrepancies observed.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Customer uses SDK version 2.14.0 with client-side embedding prefetch enabled (prefetch=true).
2) Simulate high QPS (~400 req/s) with mixed-length queries and 4 concurrent worker threads per client instance.
3) Observe /v1/rerank responses: intermittent candidate counts < requested top_k and tail latency spikes to 750-1200ms.
4) Disable prefetch on client or reduce client worker threads to 1 and re-run - issue frequency drops significantly.

investigation_notes: Initial triage: symptoms correlate with client's rollout of prefetch behavior (customer provided canary config).
Heap and thread profiles on affected replicas show an increased number of prefetch threads entering blocking syscall in close proximity to batch ingestion spikes.

Observed CPU steal and cgroup throttling on nodes hosting serving runtime + embed processes during high prefetch bursts; kernel reports high iowait to local block device used by ephemeral index cache.

Hypothesis A: aggressive prefetch threads performing synchronous disk reads for embedding warmup cause worker starvation in the rerank pool, increasing queue waits and sometimes timing out partial merging of ANN candidates.

Hypothesis B: interaction between prefetch-induced I/O and kube node autoscaling leads to transient packet loss between embed and rerank replicas causing partial candidate lists to be returned while the system falls back to best-effort merging.
Reproduction in staging with local index mirrored: enabling prefetch with 12 concurrent workers reproduces p95 spike; disabling prefetch returns baseline latency.
comments: Jordan Kim (support): Customer opened with example request IDs and SDK rollout notes at 2026-03-11T15:05Z. Requested urgent triage.
Priya Desai (oncall SRE): Assigned and started capture of pprof and iostat across affected nodes; spinning up temporary extra cpu reservation for affected pods to test mitigation. 2026-03-11T16:10Z.

Eng (runtime): Noted similar pattern to INT-4412 where background index maintenance and prefetch combined to create noisy neighbor I/O. Proposed immediate mitigation to limit concurrent prefetch threads per pod. 2026-03-12T09:23Z.

Customer (QleverSearch): Can confirm changing SDK to prefetch=false reduces error rate; however they rely on prefetch for cold start latency improvements. Seeking a fix that preserves prefetch benefits without causing rerank degradation. 2026-03-12T12:40Z.
CS (account): Requested an action plan and ETA for a fix or recommended knob configuration for Dedicated customers. 2026-03-12T14:05Z.
root_cause: Race between client-driven embedding prefetch threads and server-side ANN merge workers that led to I/O saturation on ephemeral index cache devices. Prefetch threads performed large synchronous reads, increasing iowait and causing cgroup cpu throttling; rerank merge workers were starved leading to partial candidate merges or time-limited fallbacks.
resolution_notes: Mitigations applied: 1) Deployed runtime patch limiting concurrent prefetch-handling goroutines per embed replica and converting prefetch reads to async buffered reads (PR #1892). 2) Increased ephemeral cache io scheduler tunables for Dedicated us-east pool as stopgap. 3) Recommended client-side guidance: use prefetch with max_concurrency=3 for now and upgrade SDK to 2.14.2 which includes backpressure headers. 4) Created follow-up INT task to add admission control to prevent colocating heavy prefetch customers on same node. Monitoring shows P95 returned to ~140ms for the customer after changes.
postmortem_followups: Create a permanent admission controller to limit prefetch I/O footprint per node (INT-4470)
Add an observability metric for prefetch backlog and embed read latency exposed to Console and per-customer dashboards
Document recommended prefetch client settings for Dedicated customers in KB article and include in SDK release notes
